messages:
jordan: seeing a few customers report sudden token spikes after we failed over to burst pool at ~11:02 UTC. request id: req_84f2. can someone triage?
anya: thanks — I pulled logs, looks like the client retried twice and we recorded both completion chunks as billed completions. maybe retry dedupe isn't applied after toolcall fallback.
maria: ugh. are these toolcalls? or normal completions?
anya: mix. main request with a toolcall, then the tool returned, then on retry the toolcall returned again and our metering saw two completions + the prompt. counted approx prompt=48, completion=120, twice for the same logical response.
leo: that suggests we don't tie token accounting to the original request's retry_id. router reassigns to a new worker and the metering event lacks the original retry marker.
sam: can you paste the log snippet? maybe we can repro locally.
anya: pasted logs: ```
[2026-03-20T11:02:01Z] req=req_84f2 retry=0 route=burst worker=wu-07 tokens.prompt=48 tokens.completion=120 meter.event_id=ev_9a1
[2026-03-20T11:02:02Z] req=req_84f2 retry=1 route=burst worker=wu-12 tokens.completion=118 meter.event_id=ev_9b2
```
jordan: meter.event_id differs because each worker emits its own metering. we then aggregate by req but our aggregator dedup key is req + worker, not req + retry_id.
quota-enforcer-bot: alert: org=acme corp exceeded burst-credit by 3.2k tokens during 11:02 window. policy=per-key-burst.
maria: proposed short-term fix: before billing completion tokens, check last-seen-meter.event_id for req and ignore if duplicate within 5s AND the completion sequence overlaps. but that's heuristic.
leo: long-term: include immutable request_trace_id that persists across retries and worker hops and include retry_index in metering payload. then dedupe deterministically in the metering service.
sam: impact on console: orgs see a weird "reserved vs billed" mismatch. should we expose a reserved counter when we return 429/retry semantics?
jordan: yes — UX ask: show reserved tokens for in-flight requests (temporary) and only move to billed after final success. that will reduce confusion when retries happen.
anya: telemetry gap: our per-token breakdown currently tags token_source as "prompt" or "completion" but doesn't include "toolcall" or "tool-embedded-completion". need finer taxonomy so we can debug toolcall double-counts.
maria: agree. also we should emit meter.trace: { request_trace_id, retry_index, tool_call_id, finality=true/false } as flat fields.
sam: can someone run a quick query to confirm which customers hit this? I'll open a support ticket template.
leo: running now: `SELECT sum(tokens) FROM meter WHERE request_id='req_84f2' GROUP BY meter.event_id` -> shows duplicates. will expand to orgs with similar pattern.
jordan: mitigation plan: 1) add immediate dedupe heuristic in metering service (30m hotfix) 2) add request_trace_id to router + worker (1d) 3) longer-term: expose reserved vs billed in console + docs (2w) 4) canary rollout on 10% of burst traffic (after #2).
maria: shall we gate hotfix behind a quick test? I'll write a unit test for overlapping completion ranges.
anya: also flag streaming cases: if client reconnects mid-stream we may have partial completions counted twice. need idempotent streaming tokens by sequence id.
quota-enforcer-bot: note: automated reconciliation job runs hourly; it can backfill and credit customers for double-counts but it's heavy. we should run it for affected orgs once dedupe is live.
sam: I'll draft a customer note and credits workflow. jordan — want me to sync with CS?
jordan: please do. I'll assign follow-ups in the incident board and set a canary window. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
